{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Implement the Sqoop metastore selection through externalized Spring configuration, preserving the existing default behavior while allowing a user-supplied JDBC metastore configuration.",
    "Expose bulk metrics through REST endpoints following the requested resource pattern: /metrics/counters/all, /metrics/gauges/all, and /metrics/rich-gauges/all. Preserve existing single-metric endpoints and response conventions.",
    "Use the existing Spring XD module, container, and repository abstractions wherever possible rather than introducing new parallel APIs.",
    "Implement the Boot-based ModuleRunner as a Spring Boot application with configurable module lifecycle, environment, and transport settings, while retaining compatibility with existing module definitions.",
    "Configure GemFire native authentication through documented Spring and GemFire properties, using the existing GemFire source implementation and security hooks.",
    "Implement jdbcgpfdist as a batch-oriented job that reuses the existing gpfdist sink/writer logic and adds JDBC input, batch orchestration, configuration, and restart/error handling appropriate for batch execution.",
    "Separate mock repositories from real repository integration in the test infrastructure by introducing thin repository contracts, test doubles, and explicitly scoped integration-test support.",
    "Move the Reactor-based data processor into the core repository/module structure, adapting package names, build configuration, public APIs, examples, and tests to use the core Reactor Stream API.",
    "Use automated unit and integration tests for each feature, with focused regression testing against existing behavior and REST/configuration compatibility."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The increment is implemented against an existing Spring XD codebase with a functioning build, CI process, module conventions, metrics subsystem, repository layer, GemFire integration, gpfdist sink, and Reactor module source available for reuse.",
    "The developer is responsible for implementation, automated tests, documentation updates, local verification, and integration of all eight user stories, but not for major redesign of unrelated framework components.",
    "One workday represents one person-day of productive development effort; elapsed calendar duration, parallel staffing, and external review time are excluded.",
    "U1 requires configuration and wiring changes for an alternative Sqoop metastore implementation, not development of a new database schema or a new metastore provider.",
    "For U2, the HDFS-backed module registry implementation already exists or is available in the codebase; the work is to validate the recommended configuration and add or correct user documentation and examples.",
    "For U3, the existing metrics model and serialization format can represent collections of counters, gauges, and rich-gauges without introducing a new metrics storage system.",
    "U4's unspecified scope is assumed to mean a minimal production-capable Spring Boot ModuleRunner that can start and manage a module in a container-managed environment without xd-containers, including configuration and lifecycle behavior but excluding a full replacement of all container orchestration features.",
    "U5 concerns an existing GemFire source and native GemFire authentication support; no new authentication provider, identity-management service, or authorization model is required.",
    "U6 uses existing JDBC and gpfdist abstractions where available and does not require changes to the HAWQ/GPDB server or gpfdist protocol.",
    "U7 is limited to repository coupling in the test infrastructure and does not require replacing the entire testing framework or rewriting unrelated tests.",
    "U8 moves and adapts the existing Reactor data processor implementation; it does not require creating new Reactor operators or changing the external Reactor project.",
    "Build, dependency, and compatibility issues are expected to be moderate and resolved within the stated estimates; no major undocumented platform migration is included.",
    "Documentation is limited to configuration, usage, migration, and examples directly required by these user stories."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A0",
      "activity_name": "Increment analysis and implementation design",
      "activity_description": "Inspect the existing modules, build structure, configuration conventions, metrics APIs, repository test infrastructure, GemFire integration, gpfdist sink, container lifecycle, and Reactor module. Define interfaces, compatibility constraints, implementation sequencing, and test strategy for all user stories.",
      "most_likely_effort": 4
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Configurable Sqoop metastore",
      "activity_description": "Implement external metastore selection and Spring configuration, wire the selected metastore into Sqoop startup and runtime behavior, preserve default behavior, add validation and error handling, create unit/integration tests for alternative configurations, and document the configuration.",
      "most_likely_effort": 6
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "HDFS-backed module registry documentation",
      "activity_description": "Verify the HDFS-backed module registry configuration against the current implementation, document required properties, paths, permissions, deployment considerations, and representative examples, and add documentation checks or lightweight configuration validation where appropriate.",
      "most_likely_effort": 3
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Bulk metrics REST endpoints",
      "activity_description": "Add REST handlers and service methods for retrieving all counters, gauges, and rich-gauges in one request. Define collection response behavior, empty-result behavior, error handling, endpoint compatibility, serialization tests, controller tests, and documentation/examples.",
      "most_likely_effort": 7
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Boot-based ModuleRunner",
      "activity_description": "Create the Spring Boot-based ModuleRunner entry point and configuration model, integrate module startup and shutdown lifecycle, support container-managed execution without xd-containers, handle environment and logging configuration, update packaging/build metadata, and add unit and application-context tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 12
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "GemFire native authentication support and documentation",
      "activity_description": "Adapt the GemFire source configuration to support native GemFire authentication, expose the required security properties, wire credentials and connection initialization through the existing source path, test authenticated and unauthenticated configurations, and document property locations and deployment setup.",
      "most_likely_effort": 7
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "jdbcgpfdist batch job",
      "activity_description": "Implement the JDBC reader to gpfdist writer batch job, reuse and adapt the existing gpfdist sink/writer, define job parameters and mapping configuration, support batching and failure handling, add restart/validation behavior appropriate to the existing batch framework, and create JDBC-to-gpfdist tests with mocked and integration-level boundaries.",
      "most_likely_effort": 12
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Repository test-infrastructure separation",
      "activity_description": "Refactor test support so mock repositories and real repository integrations are separate, introduce thin dependency contracts and reusable test doubles, migrate affected tests, retain focused repository integration tests, and verify that unit tests no longer require real repository infrastructure.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Reactor data processor migration to core",
      "activity_description": "Move the Reactor-based data processor into the core repository/module, update package and build dependencies, adapt APIs and module metadata, migrate examples and documentation, remove obsolete source coupling, and add unit, integration, and compatibility tests for Reactor Stream processing.",
      "most_likely_effort": 14
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Cross-feature integration and regression testing",
      "activity_description": "Run the complete build and test suite, verify configuration and packaging interactions, test REST and module startup behavior together, investigate and fix regressions across the eight stories, validate backward compatibility, and perform targeted operational smoke tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Release preparation and final documentation",
      "activity_description": "Consolidate user-facing documentation, migration notes, configuration examples, release notes, dependency updates, test evidence, and final source/build cleanup needed to deliver the increment.",
      "most_likely_effort": 3
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 84
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: Implement the Sqoop metastore selection through externalized Spring configuration, preserving the existing default behavior while allowing a user-supplied JDBC metastore configuration.

Expose bulk metrics through REST endpoints following the requested resource pattern: /metrics/counters/all, /metrics/gauges/all, and /metrics/rich-gauges/all. Preserve existing single-metric endpoints and response conventions.
Use the existing Spring XD module, container, and repository abstractions wherever possible rather than introducing new parallel APIs.

Implement the Boot-based ModuleRunner as a Spring Boot application with configurable module lifecycle, environment, and transport settings, while retaining compatibility with existing module definitions.
Configure GemFire native authentication through documented Spring and GemFire properties, using the existing GemFire source implementation and security hooks.

Implement jdbcgpfdist as a batch-oriented job that reuses the existing gpfdist sink/writer logic and adds JDBC input, batch orchestration, configuration, and restart/error handling appropriate for batch execution.
Separate mock repositories from real repository integration in the test infrastructure by introducing thin repository contracts, test doubles, and explicitly scoped integration-test support.
Move the Reactor-based data processor into the core repository/module structure, adapting package names, build configuration, public APIs, examples, and tests to use the core Reactor Stream API.
Use automated unit and integration tests for each feature, with focused regression testing against existing behavior and REST/configuration compatibility.
assumptions: The increment is implemented against an existing Spring XD codebase with a functioning build, CI process, module conventions, metrics subsystem, repository layer, GemFire integration, gpfdist sink, and Reactor module source available for reuse.

The developer is responsible for implementation, automated tests, documentation updates, local verification, and integration of all eight user stories, but not for major redesign of unrelated framework components.
One workday represents one person-day of productive development effort; elapsed calendar duration, parallel staffing, and external review time are excluded.
U1 requires configuration and wiring changes for an alternative Sqoop metastore implementation, not development of a new database schema or a new metastore provider.

For U2, the HDFS-backed module registry implementation already exists or is available in the codebase; the work is to validate the recommended configuration and add or correct user documentation and examples.
For U3, the existing metrics model and serialization format can represent collections of counters, gauges, and rich-gauges without introducing a new metrics storage system.

U4's unspecified scope is assumed to mean a minimal production-capable Spring Boot ModuleRunner that can start and manage a module in a container-managed environment without xd-containers, including configuration and lifecycle behavior but excluding a full replacement of all container orchestration features.
U5 concerns an existing GemFire source and native GemFire authentication support; no new authentication provider, identity-management service, or authorization model is required.
U6 uses existing JDBC and gpfdist abstractions where available and does not require changes to the HAWQ/GPDB server or gpfdist protocol.
U7 is limited to repository coupling in the test infrastructure and does not require replacing the entire testing framework or rewriting unrelated tests.
U8 moves and adapts the existing Reactor data processor implementation; it does not require creating new Reactor operators or changing the external Reactor project.
Build, dependency, and compatibility issues are expected to be moderate and resolved within the stated estimates; no major undocumented platform migration is included.
Documentation is limited to configuration, usage, migration, and examples directly required by these user stories.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing modules, build structure, configuration conventions, metrics APIs, repository test infrastructure, GemFire integration, gpfdist sink, container lifecycle, and Reactor module. Define interfaces, compatibility constraints, implementation sequencing, and test strategy for all user stories.

Implement external metastore selection and Spring configuration, wire the selected metastore into Sqoop startup and runtime behavior, preserve default behavior, add validation and error handling, create unit/integration tests for alternative configurations, and document the configuration.

Verify the HDFS-backed module registry configuration against the current implementation, document required properties, paths, permissions, deployment considerations, and representative examples, and add documentation checks or lightweight configuration validation where appropriate.

Add REST handlers and service methods for retrieving all counters, gauges, and rich-gauges in one request. Define collection response behavior, empty-result behavior, error handling, endpoint compatibility, serialization tests, controller tests, and documentation/examples.

Create the Spring Boot-based ModuleRunner entry point and configuration model, integrate module startup and shutdown lifecycle, support container-managed execution without xd-containers, handle environment and logging configuration, update packaging/build metadata, and add unit and application-context tests.

Implement the JDBC reader to gpfdist writer batch job, reuse and adapt the existing gpfdist sink/writer, define job parameters and mapping configuration, support batching and failure handling, add restart/validation behavior appropriate to the existing batch framework, and create JDBC-to-gpfdist tests with mocked and integration-level boundaries.

Refactor test support so mock repositories and real repository integrations are separate, introduce thin dependency contracts and reusable test doubles, migrate affected tests, retain focused repository integration tests, and verify that unit tests no longer require real repository infrastructure.

Run the complete build and test suite, verify configuration and packaging interactions, test REST and module startup behavior together, investigate and fix regressions across the eight stories, validate backward compatibility, and perform targeted operational smoke tests.
Consolidate user-facing documentation, migration notes, configuration examples, release notes, dependency updates, test evidence, and final source/build cleanup needed to deliver the increment.
